title: Spot races and edge cases
idea: A spot race happens when two gates both see the same spot free and both assign it; the fix makes the check and the claim one atomic step.

analogy.text: Two valets glance at the same empty bay and both drive in. A bay with one key on a hook lets only the valet holding it park.
analogy.breaks: A compare-and-set never blocks; a valet waits for the key.

points: Check-then-set is two steps, so the other gate can act in between.
`compareAndSet(null, id)` checks and writes in one step; one caller wins.
A losing gate moves to the next spot instead of failing the driver.
Payments use an idempotency key, so a double tap charges once.

steps.caption: Unsafe version. Gate IN-1 looks at F2-C1 for its car.
Before IN-1 writes, IN-2 looks too. The spot is still empty.
Both gates hold the answer yes. Neither knows about the other.
IN-1 writes T-1 into the spot and lifts its barrier.
IN-2 acts on its stale yes and overwrites T-1 with T-2. Both barriers lift for one spot.
Safe version. Both gates call `compareAndSet` at the same moment.
Only one call finds the spot empty and writes. Here IN-1 wins.
IN-2's call returns false. It moves on to the next spot.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier forces both gates to look before either writes, so the double assignment shows up on every run.

walk.text: Three races: unsafe on one spot, then atomic on one and two spots.
A barrier for two threads and a thread-safe list of taken spots.
Each gate tries spots in order and stops at the first it wins.
Join both threads, then sort, so the output is the same every run.
Safe: `compareAndSet` writes only if the spot is still empty.
Unsafe: look, wait for the other gate, then write on a stale answer.

code.title: Failures and retries
code.caption: Duplicate entry, unpaid exit, a declined card, a double tap and a stray retry, each handled with one atomic map call. PAYING is a short in-flight state added here so a second charge cannot start while the first is pending; LOST is left out to keep the demo short.

walk.text: The same plate enters twice, then tries to leave before paying.
Five pay calls: declined, replayed, a new key, a double tap, a stray key.
`putIfAbsent` on the plate refuses a second entry atomically.
`computeIfAbsent` stores one result per key, so a repeated key never charges again.
Demo shortcut: the mapping function holds a bin lock. With a real gateway, `putIfAbsent` PENDING, then charge outside.
`replace` moves ACTIVE to PAYING atomically; a declined card goes back to ACTIVE.
Exit needs PAID; it frees the plate so the car can return later.

pitfalls: Never check `isFree()` then set; claim with one atomic call per spot.
Do not call a slow gateway while holding a lock other gates need.
A new key after success must hit the ticket state check, not charge again.

quiz.q: What is the first line SpotRace prints?
options: It changes from run to run
quiz.why: The barrier makes both gates see F2-C1 empty before either writes. Both then write and record the spot, so it appears twice.

takeaway: Claim a spot with one atomic step; make every payment retry idempotent.
